results.title: Convert JSON to Protobuf
results.content: # JSON to Protobuf. To generate the corresponding Protobuf schema from a JSON file:. Enter the data in the "JSON" editor. The Protobuf schema will be generated and displayed in the "Protobuf" editor. You can copy it to the clipboard or download it as a file. You can also download the binary data corresponding to your JSON. One of the main advantages of Protobuf is its compact binary format, which significantly reduces the size of serialized data compared to JSON or XML, improving performance in terms of data transmission and storage. The downside of this format is that it is a binary format, making it unreadable for humans. This **online converter** from **JSON to Protobuf** allows you to easily generate the **schema** corresponding to your JSON data. It also generates the binary data corresponding to your JSON data; this result is not displayed, as it is, of course, binary data.

results.title: Protobuf schema validation surprise/questions - Schema Registry - Confluent Community
results.content: I’m testing out protobuf schemas / validation with schema registry for the first time. For a given topic, I first published a compound protobuf msg (`UserHeartRate`) which uses other msg types defined in the same .proto file as fields. Both the supporting msg definitions and the compound msg definition are defined at the top level of the file – the supporting msg definitions aren’t nested in the compound msg definition. I then attempted to publish to the same topic one of the supporting msg types (`User`), and expected this to fail since it’s not compatible with the `UserHeartRate` msg schema. So I figured maybe the supporting msg types need to be nested within the main, compound msg type to prevent this and allow only the compound type to be allowed. So I did the same exercise with a new topic using a modified version of the .proto that only had `UserHeartRate2` defined at the top level and had the supporting types nested.

results.title: Schema Evolution in Apache Avro, Protobuf, and JSON Schema - Java Code Geeks
results.content: # Schema Evolution in Apache Avro, Protobuf, and JSON Schema. This post explores how schema evolution is handled across three common serialization formats: **Apache Avro**, **Google Protobuf**, and **JSON Schema**. Changing data structures in production can break consumers that rely on an older version of the schema. Schemas are defined in JSON and describe record structures, fields, and types. **Compatibility modes in Avro (via Confluent Schema Registry):**. | Feature | Avro | Protobuf | JSON Schema |. * **Confluent Schema Registry:** Supports Avro, Protobuf, JSON Schema with version control and compatibility checks. | **Version Schemas Explicitly** | Embed a `version` field in JSON payloads to guide deserialization logic. By adopting tools like schema registries and serialization formats designed with evolution in mind, teams can decouple producers from consumers and roll out changes with confidence. Whether you pick Avro, Protobuf, or JSON Schema, the key is the same: **treat your schema like code—version it, test it, and validate it before deploying**.
